source.text: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν·

records.literal_gloss: Not store up for yourselves treasures on the earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves dig through and steal;

en.L: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal,
en.B: Do not pile up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moths and rust ruin them and thieves dig through walls and steal them.
en.R: Do not save up riches for yourselves here on earth. Moths and rust can destroy them, and robbers can break in and steal them.

es.L: No {{plural_you:atesoren|atesoréis}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tesoros sobre la tierra, donde la polilla y el óxido destruyen, y donde ladrones abren boquetes y roban;
es.B: No {{plural_you:amontonen|amontonéis}} tesoros para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en la tierra, donde la polilla y el óxido los echan a perder y los ladrones perforan las paredes y los roban.
es.R: No {{plural_you:guarden|guardéis}} riquezas para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} aquí en la tierra. La polilla y el óxido pueden destruirlas, y los ladrones pueden entrar a robarlas.

sw.L: Msijikusanyie hazina juu ya nchi, mahali ambapo nondo na kutu huziharibu, na mahali ambapo wezi hutoboa ukuta na kuiba;
sw.B: Msijilimbikizie hazina hapa duniani, ambako nondo na kutu huziharibu, na wezi hutoboa kuta na kuziiba.
sw.R: Msijikusanyie mali nyingi hapa duniani. Nondo na kutu zinaweza kuiharibu, na wezi wanaweza kuvunja nyumba na kuiiba.

decisions.choice: rust: corrosion, or the eating away of stored goods
decisions.reason: The word means "eating". It may be rust on metal, or pests eating stored food and cloth. Moths ate the fine clothes in which wealth was often kept.

decisions.choice: break in: dig through the wall
decisions.reason: Many houses had walls of mud brick, which a thief could dig through.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural 'you' ({{plural_you:atesoren|atesoréis}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}})
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the crowd, so each plural "you", pronoun or verb, is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). Where the Greek turns to the singular, as in verses 21-23, Spanish uses "tú", which has no setting.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:atesoren|atesoréis}} ... tesoros
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats one root, "treasure up treasures". "Atesorar" and "tesoros" keep the repetition at Literal; Balanced says "amontonar", as the English says "pile up".

decisions.choice: hutoboa ukuta (L, B)
decisions.reason: The verb is to dig through, since a house wall of mud brick could be broken through (meaning decision m2). "Kutoboa ukuta" says that; Readable says "kuvunja nyumba" (break into a house), as the English says "break in".

source.text: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει, καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν·

records.literal_gloss: store up but for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves not dig through nor steal;

en.L: but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not break in or steal.
en.B: Instead, pile up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where no moth or rust can ruin them and no thief can dig through and steal.
en.R: Instead, save up riches for yourselves in heaven. There, moths and rust cannot destroy them, and robbers cannot break in and steal them.

es.L: sino {{plural_you:atesoren|atesorad}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} tesoros en el cielo, donde ni la polilla ni el óxido destruyen, y donde ladrones no abren boquetes ni roban;
es.B: Más bien, {{plural_you:amontonen|amontonad}} tesoros para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en el cielo, donde ni la polilla ni el óxido los echan a perder, ni hay ladrones que perforen las paredes y los roben.
es.R: Más bien, {{plural_you:guarden|guardad}} riquezas para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en el cielo. Allí la polilla y el óxido no pueden destruirlas, y los ladrones no pueden entrar a robarlas.

sw.L: bali jikusanyieni hazina mbinguni, mahali ambapo nondo wala kutu haziharibu, na mahali ambapo wezi hawatoboi wala hawaibi;
sw.B: Badala yake, jilimbikizieni hazina mbinguni, ambako nondo wala kutu haziwezi kuziharibu, na hakuna wezi wa kutoboa kuta na kuziiba.
sw.R: Badala yake, jikusanyieni mali mbinguni. Huko nondo na kutu haziwezi kuiharibu, na wezi hawawezi kuvunja na kuiiba.

decisions.choice: treasures in heaven: what God keeps for those who give and obey
decisions.reason: Jesus tells the rich man to sell what he has and give to the poor, "and you will have treasure in heaven" (19:21). What is given away for God is kept by God.

source.text: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου, ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου.

records.literal_gloss: where for is the treasure of you, there will be also the heart of you.

en.L: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
en.B: Your heart will always be where your treasure is.
en.R: Your heart will be wherever your riches are.

es.L: Pues donde está tu tesoro, allí también estará tu corazón.
es.B: Tu corazón estará siempre donde esté tu tesoro.
es.R: Tu corazón estará dondequiera que estén tus riquezas.

sw.L: Kwa maana pale ilipo hazina yako, hapo pia moyo wako utakuwepo.
sw.B: Moyo wako utakuwa daima pale ilipo hazina yako.
sw.R: Moyo wako utakuwa mahali popote ilipo mali yako.

decisions.choice: heart: what a person loves and lives for
decisions.reason: The heart is the center of a person's will and devotion. What people value most draws their whole life after it.

decisions.choice: your: singular here, after the plural of 6:19-20
decisions.reason: The saying is put to each listener personally.

decisions.choice: tu, with no plural_you span
decisions.reason: The Greek turns from the plural of 6:19-20 to the singular here (meaning decision m2). Spanish shows it with "tu", which has no setting, as the English cannot.

source.text: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός.

records.literal_gloss: The lamp of the body is the eye.

en.L: The lamp of the body is the eye.
en.B: The eye is the lamp of the body.
en.R: Your eye is like a lamp for your body.

es.L: La lámpara del cuerpo es el ojo.
es.B: El ojo es la lámpara del cuerpo.
es.R: Tu ojo es como una lámpara para tu cuerpo.

sw.L: Taa ya mwili ndiyo jicho.
sw.B: Jicho ni taa ya mwili.
sw.R: Jicho lako ni kama taa kwa mwili wako.

decisions.choice: the eye as a lamp: the way light reaches the whole person
decisions.reason: People spoke of the eye as letting light in, or as a lamp shining out. Jesus uses the picture for how a person looks at life and possessions.

source.text: ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται·

records.literal_gloss: If therefore is the eye of you single, whole the body of you full of light will be;

en.L: So if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light,
en.B: So if your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
en.R: If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.

es.L: Si, pues, tu ojo está sano, todo tu cuerpo será luminoso;
es.B: Así que, si tu ojo está sano, tendrás todo el cuerpo lleno de luz.
es.R: Si tus ojos son buenos, todo tu cuerpo se llenará de luz.

sw.L: Ikiwa basi jicho lako ni zima, mwili wako wote utakuwa wenye nuru;
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, jicho lako likiwa zima, mwili wako wote utajaa nuru.
sw.R: Macho yako yakiwa mazuri, mwili wako wote utajaa nuru.

decisions.choice: healthy: sound, single, and so generous
decisions.reason: The word means single or undivided, and was used of generosity. Between sayings about treasure (6:19-21) and money (6:24), a healthy eye is an undivided devotion that shows itself in generosity.

decisions.choice: luminoso (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek adjective means "full of light", and its pair in verse 23 "full of darkness". Literal says "luminoso" and "oscuro", one word each, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: zima (L, B); mazuri (R)
decisions.reason: The word means sound or single, and so perhaps generous (meaning decision m1, uncertain). "Zima" is whole and healthy; "safi" (clean) is the familiar word but says neither. Readable says "mazuri" (good), as the English says "good".

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται.

records.literal_gloss: if but the eye of you evil is, whole the body of you full of darkness will be.

en.L: but if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness.
en.B: But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness.
en.R: But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness.

es.L: pero si tu ojo es malo, todo tu cuerpo será oscuro.
es.B: Pero si tu ojo es malo, tendrás todo el cuerpo lleno de oscuridad.
es.R: Pero si tus ojos son malos, todo tu cuerpo se llenará de oscuridad.

sw.L: lakini ikiwa jicho lako ni ovu, mwili wako wote utakuwa wenye giza.
sw.B: Lakini jicho lako likiwa baya, mwili wako wote utajaa giza.
sw.R: Lakini macho yako yakiwa mabaya, mwili wako wote utajaa giza.

decisions.choice: a bad eye: an evil eye, that is, a stingy and greedy spirit
decisions.reason: In Hebrew an "evil eye" means a grudging, greedy attitude (Deuteronomy 15:9; Proverbs 28:22), and Jesus uses the phrase that way in 20:15.

decisions.choice: malo
decisions.reason: A "bad eye" was an evil eye, a stingy and greedy spirit, as well as a sick one (meaning decision m1, uncertain). Spanish "malo" can be said of an eye that does not see well and of a person who does wrong, so it keeps both.

decisions.choice: ovu (L); baya (B); mabaya (R)
decisions.reason: A "bad eye" was an evil eye, a stingy and greedy spirit (meaning decision m1, uncertain). Literal says "ovu" (evil), the Greek word; "bovu" would mean only a defective eye. Balanced and Readable say "baya" (bad), which covers both, as the English does.

source.text: εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν, τὸ σκότος πόσον.

records.literal_gloss: If therefore the light the in you darkness is, the darkness how great.

en.L: If then the light that [is] in you is darkness, how great the darkness!
en.B: So if the light inside you is really darkness, how deep that darkness is!
en.R: If the light inside you is really darkness, then you are in very great darkness.

es.L: Si, pues, la luz que [hay] en ti es oscuridad, ¡cuán grande la oscuridad!
es.B: Así que, si la luz que hay dentro de ti es en realidad oscuridad, ¡qué profunda es esa oscuridad!
es.R: Si la luz que hay dentro de ti es en realidad oscuridad, entonces estás en una oscuridad muy grande.

sw.L: Kama basi ile nuru iliyomo ndani yako ni giza, lo, ni giza kuu kiasi gani!
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, ikiwa nuru iliyo ndani yako kwa kweli ni giza, giza hilo ni zito mno!
sw.R: Ikiwa nuru iliyo ndani yako kwa kweli ni giza, basi uko katika giza kubwa sana.

decisions.choice: the light in you is darkness: the means of seeing has become blind
decisions.reason: If what should guide a person is itself corrupted by greed, there is nothing left to show the way.

source.text: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει.

records.literal_gloss: No one is able two masters to serve; either for the one he will hate and the other he will love, or one he will hold to and the other he will despise.

en.L: No one can serve two masters, for either {{gender:they|he}} will hate the one and love the other, or {{gender:they|he}} will be devoted to one and despise the other.
en.B: No one can serve two masters. Either {{gender:they|he}} will hate one and love the other, or {{gender:they|he}} will be loyal to one and look down on the other.
en.R: No one can serve two masters at the same time. {{gender:They|He}} will hate one master and love the other, or {{gender:they|he}} will be loyal to one and not care about the other.

es.L: Nadie puede servir a dos señores, porque o bien odiará al uno y amará al otro, o bien se apegará a uno y despreciará al otro.
es.B: Nadie puede servir a dos amos. O bien odiará a uno y amará al otro, o bien será leal a uno y menospreciará al otro.
es.R: Nadie puede servir a dos amos al mismo tiempo. Odiará a uno y amará al otro, o será fiel a uno y no le importará el otro.

sw.L: Hakuna anayeweza kuwatumikia mabwana wawili; kwa maana ama atamchukia mmoja na kumpenda mwingine, ama atashikamana na mmoja na kumdharau mwingine.
sw.B: Hakuna mtu anayeweza kuwatumikia mabwana wawili. Atamchukia mmoja na kumpenda mwingine, au atakuwa mwaminifu kwa mmoja na kumdharau mwingine.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu anayeweza kuwatumikia mabwana wawili kwa wakati mmoja. Atamchukia mmoja na kumpenda mwingine, au atakuwa mwaminifu kwa mmoja na kumpuuza mwingine.

decisions.choice: serve: serve as a slave, who belongs wholly to a master
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of slaves. A slave owned by two masters could not give both full service; Jesus uses the picture of total loyalty.

decisions.choice: hate ... love: prefer one and reject the other
decisions.reason: In Hebrew idiom "love" and "hate" can mean choosing one over the other (Genesis 29:30-31; Malachi 1:2-3).

decisions.choice: serve
decisions.reason: "Serve" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it for the slave words; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that this is a slave's service to a master, and Literal says "serve" too.

decisions.choice: señores (L); amos (B, R)
decisions.reason: This is a slave's service to a master (meaning decision m1). "Amo" is the master who owns a servant; Literal keeps "señor", the plain sense of the Greek word.

decisions.choice: odiará, amará, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "they" with "he" as the traditional form. Spanish needs no subject pronoun, so there is nothing for the setting to change. The same with "su vida" in verse 27.

source.text: οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.

records.literal_gloss: Not you are able God to serve and mammon.

en.L: You cannot serve God and mammon.
en.B: You cannot serve both God and money.
en.R: You cannot serve God and money at the same time.

es.L: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} servir a Dios y a Mamón.
es.B: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} servir a la vez a Dios y al dinero.
es.R: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} servir a Dios y al dinero al mismo tiempo.

sw.L: Hamwezi kumtumikia Mungu na Mamona.
sw.B: Hamwezi kumtumikia Mungu na fedha pia.
sw.R: Hamwezi kumtumikia Mungu na pesa kwa wakati mmoja.

decisions.choice: mammon: wealth and possessions, spoken of as a master
decisions.reason: Mammon is an Aramaic word for wealth or property. Jesus pictures it as a rival lord who claims a person's service.

decisions.choice: mammon (L); money (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic word. Balanced and Readable use the plain English word.

decisions.choice: serve
decisions.reason: "Serve" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it for the slave words and as in the first half of 6:24, where the meaning decision says this is a slave's service to a master; Literal says "serve" too.

decisions.choice: Mamón (L), capitalized; el dinero (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic word for wealth, spoken of as a master (meaning decision m1), as the English does. The capital makes it read as the name of a master and keeps it apart from the everyday word "mamón".

decisions.choice: Mamona (L); fedha (B); pesa (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic word for wealth, spoken of as a master (meaning decision m1), as the English does. Balanced and Readable say money: "fedha" in the careful register, "pesa" in the everyday one.

source.text: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν· μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε· οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστι τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος;

records.literal_gloss: Because of this I say to you, not be anxious [for] the life of you what you will eat, nor [for] the body of you what you will put on; not the life more is than the food and the body [than] the clothing?

en.L: Therefore I tell you, do not be anxious about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on. Is not life more than food, and the body [more] than clothing?
en.B: That is why I tell you not to worry about your life, about what you will eat, or about your body, about what you will wear. Is life not more than food, and the body more than clothes?
en.R: So I tell you, do not worry about having enough food to stay alive or enough clothes to wear. Your life is more important than food, and your body is more important than clothes.

es.L: Por esto {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: no {{plural_you:se inquieten|os inquietéis}} por {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida, qué {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}}, ni por {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo, qué {{plural_you:vestirán|vestiréis}}. ¿No es la vida más que el sustento, y el cuerpo [más] que la vestimenta?
es.B: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} por {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida, por lo que {{plural_you:van|vais}} a comer, ni por {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo, por lo que {{plural_you:van a ponerse|vais a poneros}}. ¿No es la vida más que la comida, y el cuerpo más que la ropa?
es.R: Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} por tener suficiente comida para vivir ni suficiente ropa que ponerse. {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} vida es más importante que la comida, y {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo es más importante que la ropa.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo nawaambia, msiwe na wasiwasi juu ya uhai wenu, mtakula nini, wala juu ya mwili wenu, mtavaa nini. Je, uhai si mkubwa kuliko chakula, na mwili [mkubwa] kuliko mavazi?
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu nawaambia: msiwe na wasiwasi kuhusu uhai wenu, kwamba mtakula nini, wala kuhusu miili yenu, kwamba mtavaa nini. Je, uhai si wa thamani kuliko chakula, na mwili kuliko mavazi?
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nawaambia, msiwe na wasiwasi kuhusu kupata chakula cha kuwaweka hai au nguo za kuvaa. Uhai wenu ni muhimu kuliko chakula, na miili yenu ni muhimu kuliko nguo.

decisions.choice: be anxious: worry, be troubled in mind
decisions.reason: The verb is about anxiety, not about planning. Jesus does not forbid working for food (the birds still look for theirs) but fretting over it.

decisions.choice: therefore: because you cannot serve both God and money
decisions.reason: Worry over food and clothes is the form that serving money takes for the poor.

decisions.choice: what you will eat, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: what you will eat or what you will drink, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "or what you will drink" (compare 6:31). The evidence is divided. Reviewers should check it against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled. Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Is not life more than food?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes; Readable gives the answer.

decisions.choice: inquietarse (L); preocuparse (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal says "inquietarse", to be anxious, and Balanced and Readable the everyday "preocuparse". Each level keeps its word for this verb through verse 34.

decisions.choice: uhai
decisions.reason: Here the word is the life that food keeps going. "Uhai" is being alive; "uzima" is kept for life itself, as in eternal life, and "maisha" is a lifetime or a way of living.

decisions.choice: kuwa na wasiwasi at every level
decisions.reason: The English says "be anxious" at Literal and "worry" at Balanced and Readable. Swahili "kuwa na wasiwasi" is both, so every level keeps it for this verb through verse 34, and the repetition stays visible.

source.text: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας, καὶ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά· οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Look at the birds of the heaven, that not they sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and the Father of you the heavenly feeds them; not you much are worth more than they?

en.L: Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they?
en.B: Look at the birds in the sky. They do not plant or harvest or store food in barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth far more than they are?
en.R: Look at the birds. They do not plant seeds or gather crops or store food in barns. But your Father in heaven feeds them. You are worth much more than birds.

es.L: {{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}} en los pájaros del cielo: no siembran, tampoco siegan ni almacenan en graneros, y {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre celestial los alimenta. ¿No {{plural_you:son|sois}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} de mucho más valor que ellos?
es.B: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} los pájaros que vuelan por el cielo. No siembran ni cosechan ni guardan comida en graneros, y aun así {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre celestial los alimenta. ¿Acaso no {{plural_you:valen|valéis}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} muchísimo más que ellos?
es.R: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} los pájaros. No siembran semillas, ni recogen cosechas, ni guardan comida en graneros. Pero {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que está en el cielo les da de comer. {{plural_you:Ustedes valen|Vosotros valéis}} mucho más que los pájaros.

sw.L: Waangalieni kwa makini ndege wa angani: hawapandi mbegu, hawavuni, wala hawaweki chochote ghalani, nao Baba yenu wa mbinguni huwapa chakula. Je, ninyi hamna thamani kubwa zaidi kuliko wao?
sw.B: Tazameni ndege wanaoruka angani. Hawapandi wala hawavuni, wala hawahifadhi chakula ghalani, na bado Baba yenu wa mbinguni huwalisha. Je, ninyi hamna thamani kubwa kuliko wao?
sw.R: Waangalieni ndege. Hawapandi mbegu, hawavuni mazao, wala hawahifadhi chakula ghalani. Lakini Baba yenu aliye mbinguni huwapa chakula. Ninyi mna thamani kubwa kuliko ndege.

decisions.choice: from the lesser to the greater: if God feeds birds, he will care for his children
decisions.reason: The argument runs from the smaller case to the larger, a common Jewish way of reasoning. Birds do not farm, yet God provides; disciples who do work need not fret.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Are you not worth much more?
decisions.reason: As in 6:25.

source.text: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα;

records.literal_gloss: Who but of you being anxious is able to add to the span of life of him cubit one?

en.L: And which of you by being anxious can add one cubit to {{gender:their|his}} span of life?
en.B: Can any of you add a single hour to your life by worrying?
en.R: You cannot add even one hour to your life by worrying about it.

es.L: ¿Y quién de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, por inquietarse, puede añadir un codo a la duración de su vida?
es.B: ¿Puede alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} añadir una sola hora a su vida a fuerza de preocuparse?
es.R: No {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} añadir ni una hora a {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida con la preocupación.

sw.L: Na ni nani kati yenu ambaye, kwa kuwa na wasiwasi, anaweza kuongeza dhiraa moja kwa muda wa maisha yake?
sw.B: Je, kuna yeyote kati yenu anayeweza kuongeza hata saa moja kwenye maisha yake kwa kuwa na wasiwasi?
sw.R: Hamwezi kuongeza hata saa moja kwenye maisha yenu kwa kuwa na wasiwasi.

decisions.choice: add a cubit to the span of life: lengthen life even a little
alternatives: add a cubit to one's height
decisions.reason: The word can mean length of life or stature, and a cubit is a measure of about eighteen inches. Adding a cubit to one's height would be no small thing, so a little more life is the likelier sense: worry cannot add even a moment.

decisions.choice: a single hour
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the picture of a measure into one of time, as the meaning note explains. Literal keeps "cubit".

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled. Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

decisions.choice: dhiraa moja (L)
decisions.reason: Swahili has its own word for the cubit, the length of a forearm, so Literal keeps the measure as the English Literal does. Balanced and Readable speak of an hour, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε;

records.literal_gloss: And about clothing why are you anxious?

en.L: And why are you anxious about clothing?
en.B: And why do you worry about clothes?
en.R: And why do you worry about clothes?

es.L: Y por el vestido, ¿por qué {{plural_you:se inquietan|os inquietáis}}?
es.B: ¿Y por qué {{plural_you:se preocupan|os preocupáis}} por la ropa?
es.R: ¿Y por qué {{plural_you:se preocupan|os preocupáis}} por la ropa?

sw.L: Na kuhusu mavazi, kwa nini mna wasiwasi?
sw.B: Na kwa nini mnakuwa na wasiwasi juu ya mavazi?
sw.R: Na kwa nini mnakuwa na wasiwasi kuhusu nguo?

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled. Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

source.text: καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν· οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν·

records.literal_gloss: Consider the lilies of the field how they grow; not they labor nor spin;

en.L: Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not labor or spin,
en.B: Think about how the wildflowers grow. They neither toil nor spin thread.
en.R: Look at how the wildflowers in the fields grow. They do not work or make clothes for themselves.

es.L: {{plural_you:Aprendan|Aprended}} de los lirios del campo cómo crecen: no se fatigan ni hilan;
es.B: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en cómo crecen las flores silvestres. No se afanan en el trabajo ni hilan.
es.R: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} cómo crecen las flores silvestres en los campos. No trabajan ni se hacen ropa.

sw.L: Jifunzeni kutoka kwa maua ya kondeni jinsi yanavyokua: hayajitaabishi wala hayasokoti nyuzi;
sw.B: Fikirieni jinsi maua ya porini yanavyoota. Hayajitaabishi kwa kazi wala hayasokoti nyuzi.
sw.R: Tazameni jinsi maua ya porini yanavyokua mashambani. Hayafanyi kazi wala hayajishonei nguo.

decisions.choice: the lilies of the field: wild flowers in general
decisions.reason: The word names lilies, but in this setting it covers the bright flowers of Galilee's hillsides, which grow wild.

decisions.choice: labor, spin: the work of men in the fields and of women making cloth
decisions.reason: The birds do not do men's work (6:26); the flowers do not do women's work.

decisions.choice: wildflowers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is meant; Literal keeps "lilies".

decisions.choice: maua ya kondeni (L); maua ya porini (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means wild flowers in general (meaning decision m1). Swahili "yungiyungi" is the water lily, which is not what is meant, so Literal says "maua" (flowers) too.

source.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.

records.literal_gloss: I say but to you that not even Solomon in all the glory of him was clothed as one of these.

en.L: But I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
en.B: But I tell you, Solomon in all his glory was never dressed as beautifully as one of them.
en.R: But I tell you, even King Solomon with all his riches and glory did not have clothes as beautiful as these flowers.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ni Salomón, en toda su gloria, estuvo vestido como uno de estos.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ni Salomón, con toda su gloria, se vistió jamás con tanta belleza como uno de ellos.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ni siquiera el rey Salomón, con todas sus riquezas y su gloria, tuvo ropa tan hermosa como estas flores.

sw.L: Lakini nawaambia, hata Sulemani, katika utukufu wake wote, hakujivika kama ua moja kati ya haya.
sw.B: Lakini nawaambia, Sulemani pamoja na utukufu wake wote hakuwahi kuvaa mavazi mazuri kama ua mojawapo kati ya hayo.
sw.R: Lakini nawaambia, hata Mfalme Sulemani, pamoja na utajiri na utukufu wake wote, hakuwa na nguo nzuri kama maua haya.

decisions.choice: Solomon in all his glory: Israel's richest king
decisions.reason: Solomon's wealth and splendor were famous (1 Kings 10:4-7, 23).

source.text: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν, οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι;

records.literal_gloss: If but the grass of the field today being and tomorrow into an oven being thrown the God thus clothes, not much more you, little-faiths?

en.L: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which is [here] today and tomorrow is thrown into an oven, [will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}] not much more [clothe] you, you of little faith?
en.B: If that is how God clothes the wild grass, which is here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not clothe you much more, you who have so little faith?
en.R: God dresses the grass in the fields like that. The grass is there today, and tomorrow it is burned in an oven. So God will surely give you clothes. Your faith is so small!

es.L: Pero si la hierba del campo, que hoy está [aquí] y mañana es arrojada al horno, Dios la viste así, ¿no [{{plural_you:los|os}} vestirá] mucho más a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, [gente] de poca fe?
es.B: Si así es como Dios viste a la hierba silvestre, que hoy está aquí y mañana se echa al horno, ¿no {{plural_you:los|os}} vestirá mucho más a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} tan poca fe?
es.R: Dios viste así a la hierba del campo. La hierba está allí hoy, y mañana la queman en un horno. Así que Dios, sin duda, {{plural_you:les|os}} dará ropa a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. ¡Qué poca fe {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}!

sw.L: Ikiwa basi Mungu anayavalisha namna hii majani ya shambani, yaliyoko leo na kesho yanatupwa tanuruni, [je, hatawavalisha] ninyi zaidi sana, enyi wenye imani ndogo?
sw.B: Ikiwa Mungu huyavalisha hivyo majani ya porini, ambayo leo yapo na kesho yanatupwa tanuruni, je, hatawavalisha ninyi zaidi sana, enyi wenye imani ndogo?
sw.R: Mungu huyavalisha majani ya porini namna hiyo. Majani hayo yapo leo, na kesho yanachomwa katika tanuru. Kwa hiyo hakika Mungu atawapa ninyi nguo. Imani yenu ni ndogo mno!

decisions.choice: thrown into an oven: dried grass was used as fuel
decisions.reason: Wood was scarce, and dried grass and weeds fired the clay ovens used for baking.

decisions.choice: you of little faith: people who trust God too little
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this word for the disciples when their trust gives way (8:26; 14:31; 16:8). It is a rebuke to believers.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: will he not much more clothe you?
decisions.reason: As in 6:25.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on vestirá (will he clothe)
decisions.reason: The English "he" takes the setting. Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ending, where there is nothing to capitalise, so the setting has no word here; "su" in verse 33 carries it.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on hatawavalisha (will he not clothe)
decisions.reason: The English "he" takes the setting. Swahili carries the subject in the verb prefix, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, such as "yake" in verse 33.

source.text: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες· Τί φάγωμεν;

records.literal_gloss: Not therefore be anxious saying, What shall we eat?

en.L: So do not be anxious, saying, 'What shall we eat?'
en.B: So do not worry and say, 'What will we eat?'
en.R: So do not worry and say, 'What will we eat?'

es.L: Así pues, no {{plural_you:se inquieten|os inquietéis}} diciendo: “¿Qué comeremos?”,
es.B: Así que no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} ni {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: “¿Qué vamos a comer?”,
es.R: Así que no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} diciendo: “¿Qué vamos a comer?”,

sw.L: Basi msiwe na wasiwasi mkisema, 'Tutakula nini?'
sw.B: Kwa hiyo msiwe na wasiwasi na kusema, 'Tutakula nini?'
sw.R: Kwa hiyo msiwe na wasiwasi mkiulizana, 'Tutakula nini?'

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled. Balanced and Readable use the everyday word.

source.text: ἤ· Τί πίωμεν;

records.literal_gloss: Or, What shall we drink?

en.L: or, 'What shall we drink?'
en.B: or, 'What will we drink?'
en.R: or, 'What will we drink?'

es.L: o: “¿Qué beberemos?”,
es.B: o: “¿Qué vamos a beber?”,
es.R: o: “¿Qué vamos a beber?”,

sw.L: au, 'Tutakunywa nini?'
sw.B: au, 'Tutakunywa nini?'
sw.R: au, 'Tutakunywa nini?'

decisions.choice: the second of three anxious questions
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT marks each question as its own sentence. Together they repeat the worries of 6:25.

source.text: ἤ· Τί περιβαλώμεθα;

records.literal_gloss: Or, What shall we put on?

en.L: or, 'What shall we wear?'
en.B: or, 'What will we wear?'
en.R: or, 'What will we wear?'

es.L: o: “¿Con qué nos vestiremos?”.
es.B: o: “¿Qué nos vamos a poner?”.
es.R: o: “¿Qué ropa vamos a ponernos?”.

sw.L: au, 'Tutavaa nini?'
sw.B: au, 'Tutavaa nini?'
sw.R: au, 'Tutavaa nguo gani?'

decisions.choice: the third of the anxious questions
decisions.reason: As in the previous sentence.

decisions.choice: the three questions joined, with a comma after the first two
decisions.reason: The three anxious questions form one list (meaning decision m1). Spanish closes a quoted question with "?”" and goes on with a comma, so the first two records end with a comma and the third with a full stop.

source.text: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν· οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων.

records.literal_gloss: All for these things the Gentiles seek after; knows for the Father of you the heavenly that you need these all.

en.L: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.
en.B: The pagans chase after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.
en.R: People who do not know God are always trying to get these things. But your Father in heaven knows that you need them.

es.L: Porque todas estas cosas las buscan con afán los gentiles; pues {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre celestial sabe que {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} todas ellas.
es.B: Los gentiles andan tras todas estas cosas, y {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre celestial sabe que las {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} todas.
es.R: La gente que no conoce a Dios siempre está tratando de conseguir estas cosas. Pero {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que está en el cielo sabe que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} las {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana mambo hayo yote watu wa mataifa huyakimbilia; tena Baba yenu wa mbinguni anafahamu kwamba mnayahitaji yote hayo.
sw.B: Watu wa mataifa huhangaikia mambo hayo yote, na Baba yenu wa mbinguni anajua kwamba mnayahitaji yote.
sw.R: Watu wasiomjua Mungu hujitahidi siku zote kupata vitu hivi. Lakini Baba yenu aliye mbinguni anajua kwamba mnavihitaji.

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: people who do not know the God of Israel
decisions.reason: As in 6:7. Those who have no Father in heaven to trust must strive for these things on their own.

decisions.choice: people who do not know God
decisions.reason: As in 5:47.

source.text: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Seek but first the kingdom and the righteousness of him, and these things all will be added to you.

en.L: But seek first the kingdom and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
en.B: Above all, seek the kingdom and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness, and you will be given all these things as well.
en.R: Above everything else, look for God's kingdom and do what is righteous in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes. Then God will give you all these other things too.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:busquen|buscad}} ante todo el reino y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} justicia, y todo esto {{plural_you:les|os}} será añadido.
es.B: Por encima de todo, {{plural_you:busquen|buscad}} el reino y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} justicia, y todas estas cosas {{plural_you:se les|se os}} darán también.
es.R: Antes que cualquier otra cosa, {{plural_you:busquen|buscad}} el reino de Dios y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} lo que es justo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ojos. Entonces Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} dará también todas estas otras cosas.

sw.L: Lakini kwanza tafuteni ufalme na haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, nayo mambo haya yote mtapewa kwa nyongeza.
sw.B: Zaidi ya yote, utafuteni ufalme na haki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, nanyi mtapewa mambo haya yote pia.
sw.R: Kuliko kitu kingine chochote, tafuteni ufalme wa Mungu na kutenda yaliyo haki machoni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}. Ndipo Mungu atawapa vitu vingine hivi vyote pia.

decisions.choice: his righteousness: the right living God requires, and God's justice
alternatives: the righteousness God credits to believers
decisions.reason: As throughout the sermon (5:6, 20; 6:1), righteousness is doing God's will. "His" is the Father of 6:32.

decisions.choice: the kingdom and his righteousness, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the kingdom of God and his righteousness, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "the kingdom of God". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: will be added: God will give them
decisions.reason: The passive points to God, as often in Jesus's sayings (5:4).

decisions.choice: God's kingdom; God will give you
decisions.reason: Readable names God.

source.text: μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει αὑτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Not therefore be anxious for the tomorrow, the for tomorrow will be anxious of itself; sufficient to the day the trouble of it.

en.L: So do not be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious about itself; sufficient for the day [is] its own trouble.
en.B: So do not be troubled about tomorrow; tomorrow can take care of its own worries. Today's trouble is enough for today.
en.R: So do not worry about tomorrow. Tomorrow will have its own worries. Each day has enough trouble in it.

es.L: Así que no {{plural_you:se inquieten|os inquietéis}} por el mañana, porque el mañana se inquietará por sí mismo; suficiente [es] para el día su propia aflicción.
es.B: Así que no {{plural_you:se angustien|os angustiéis}} por el mañana; el mañana sabrá ocuparse de sus propias preocupaciones. A cada día le basta con sus propios problemas.
es.R: Así que no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} por el día de mañana. Mañana tendrá sus propias preocupaciones. Cada día ya tiene bastantes problemas.

sw.L: Basi msiwe na wasiwasi kwa ajili ya kesho, kwa maana kesho itakuwa na wasiwasi wake yenyewe; inaitosha siku taabu yake.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo msiwe na wasiwasi kuhusu kesho; kesho itashughulikia mahangaiko yake yenyewe. Taabu za leo zinatosha kwa leo.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo msiwe na wasiwasi kuhusu kesho. Kesho itakuwa na wasiwasi wake. Kila siku ina taabu za kutosha.

decisions.choice: tomorrow will be anxious about itself: take each day's troubles as they come
decisions.reason: The saying is a proverb. It does not promise an easy tomorrow; it forbids carrying tomorrow's load today.
